en: Now, therefore, I shall fully explain the accomplishment of the five nectars (*pañcāmṛta*).
By which correct procedure there arises the fruit of all accomplishments.
One should take [the substance] produced from the womb of a Brāhmaṇī,
preserved according to the ritual rule.
Therefore, that which is known by the name Vairocana is also considered to be the accomplishment of renown.
Dark-complexioned, with beautiful limbs and eyes with black pupils—
from that, one born of the Jewel family shall obtain and accomplish what is concealed in the Sūtra.
A fortunate young lotus-like woman, having been fully gratified and protected with urine, food,
and drink, the wise man should offer everything to her.
At that moment, one should perform the *kunduru* rite and cause the semen to be taken by one another;
from that, the lineage of actors (*naṭakula*) arises, and the Tathāgata likewise pervades it.
By means of the previously described procedure, complete accomplishment is attained;
the first flower is praised, for it is proclaimed to bestow vitality and splendor.
If, having attained the samaya, one should always cause Mātaṅgī to be tasted;
likewise, the wise one should cause her to accept meat and blood.
The five-pronged [vajra], as it is obtained, is said here to be the best when its [impurities] have been destroyed;
if the practitioner who desires accomplishment should obtain and grasp it.
The wise one should cause [the practitioner] to consume his own flesh, as well as the flesh of an elephant, cow, human, and chicken.
The five lamps have been explained according to the words of Vajrasattva;
one should strive for this subject matter as it has been attained by the ten classes of beings.
On the tenth lunar day,
one should apply fragrant substances mixed together; however, one should not cause [the ritual] to be performed in secret,
for secrecy is not [required].
The practitioner should properly fashion the pill, keeping it secret.
At that very moment, let the food and drink, especially in abundance, be established in the midst of the Gaṇas; thereafter, one should commence the ritual action.
The recitation of the mantra of the fourfold group (*gaṇa*), which brings about the arising of the fruit of all ritual actions,
as well as the recitation of the mantra and likewise meditative absorption (*dhyāna*).
The elixir of the body is the supreme, imperishable means of attaining perfection.
One should daily consume the pill, which bestows the fruit of all desires;
in the application of all ritual actions, the state of the Khecarī is attained.
Thus ends the sixteenth chapter, the exposition of the method for the practice of the five nectars, in the glorious *Samvarodaya-mahātantra*.
